conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: GapPrimitive
candidates.quote: if the market is in a bull trend and today's low is above the high of yesterday, then today gapped up
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a true gap between consecutive bars (bar's low above prior bar's high for a bull gap, or high below prior bar's low for a bear gap).
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (chart feature; trade with the gap direction)
notes: Same definition as R08-04 GapUpBar; redefined per-chapter per convention.

candidates.name: OpenAboveCloseGapPrimitive
candidates.quote: Occasionally, the open of a bar on a 5 minute chart will be above the close of the prior bar, and this is often a subtle indication of strength.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar's open is above the prior bar's close (a weaker, intrabar-only 'gap' usable on any timeframe, not just at session boundaries).
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (subtle strength indication, not an order trigger by itself)

candidates.name: ConsecutiveOpenGapsStrengthFilter
candidates.quote: For example, if there are two or three of these gaps on consecutive bull trend bars, the bulls are likely strong.
candidates.description: Filter: treat the trend as strong when N consecutive bull trend bars each opened above the prior bar's close (mirrored for bear).
candidates.pseudocode: for i in 0..consecutiveBars-1: open[i] > close[i+1] && close[i] > open[i]

candidates.name: TrendBarActsAsGapPrimitive
candidates.quote: Because all trend bars are gaps, traders can see intraday equivalents of the traditional gaps that are so common on daily charts... a breakout is a variant of a gap.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a trend bar b functions as a gap when the bar after it does not overlap the bar before it (low[b-1] and high[b+1] leave a gap), even though no traditional gap prints on the chart.

complexity.reason: needs the identified trend bar plus its neighbors, evaluated once the following bar closes

notes: This is the general form of R08-08's 'first non-trend bar defines gap top' construction, phrased around any single trend bar rather than a whole breakout leg.

candidates.name: MicroMeasuringGapTarget
candidates.quote: A very common type of gap occurs in any three consecutive trending bars on any chart. For example, if these three bars are trending up and the low of bar 3 is at or above the high of bar 1, there is a gap and it can act as a measuring gap or a breakaway gap.
candidates.description: Around any single trend bar b (or any three consecutive same-direction trend bars) with a gap per R06-04: gapMid = (high[b-1] + low[b+1]) / 2; legStart = lowest low over legLookback bars ending at or before b; target = gapMid + (gapMid - legStart); exit/take profit when price reaches it.
candidates.pseudocode: gapMid = (high[b-1] + low[b+1]) / 2; legStart = lowest(low, legLookback)[b]; target = gapMid + (gapMid - legStart); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: target persists from a detected micro-gap bar and needs the start of the leg containing it, same structure as R08-05/R08-09

notes: Micro measured moves are least reliable in the first few bars of a brand-new trend (book: 'the market will usually extend much further'); see R06-06.

candidates.name: EarlyDayGapTargetUnreliableFilter
candidates.quote: if the average daily range in the Emini has been about 12 points and after about an hour into the day the range is only three points, the gap formed by a breakout would lead to a target that would result in a range for the day of only six points... traders should not be taking profits at the measured move target
candidates.description: Filter: distrust a gap-based measured-move target (do not fade/take profits there) when today's range so far is a small fraction of the average daily range, since the trend is likely to extend well past it.
candidates.pseudocode: todaysRangeSoFar = highest(high, barsToday) - lowest(low, barsToday); todaysRangeSoFar < minRangeFraction * avgDailyRange(adrLookback) => distrustGapTarget

complexity.reason: needs a session-relative range accumulator and an average-daily-range design decision

candidates.name: GapDistanceFractionOfADRFilter
candidates.quote: When the distance from the start of the leg to the breakout gap (breakaway gap) is about a third to a half of an average daily range, its middle often leads to a measured move projection where traders might take profits or even reverse their positions.
candidates.description: Filter: trust a gap-based measured-move target more when the leg height up to the gap falls within [minFrac, maxFrac] of the average daily range.
candidates.pseudocode: legHeight = gapMid - legStart; legHeight >= minFrac * avgDailyRange(adrLookback) && legHeight <= maxFrac * avgDailyRange(adrLookback)

complexity.reason: compares an already-computed leg height against an average-daily-range window

candidates.name: GapFilledSignalsWeakness
candidates.quote: If, before going much higher, the market trades back down to below the high of the bar before the gap, traders will see that as a sign of weakness and will think that the gap might represent exhaustion, which is a type of buy climax.
candidates.description: Once a bull gap's bottom (the high of the bar before the gap) is closed below, treat the gap as filled/exhaustion and exit the remaining long swing.
candidates.pseudocode: gapBottom = high of the bar before the identified gap; close[0] < gapBottom - toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: exit/reverse on the close that fills the gap

complexity.reason: needs the remembered boundary of a specific identified gap

candidates.name: FirstEmaGapBarShortEntry
candidates.quote: if there is a strong bear trend and the market finally rallies above the moving average, the first bar in that rally that has a low above the moving average is a first moving average gap bar. Traders will place a sell stop order at one tick below the low of that bar to go short
candidates.description: In a bear trend, the first bar of a countertrend rally whose low closes above the EMA is a 'first moving average gap bar'; sell one tick below its low, trailing the stop down to one tick below each new bar's low until filled.
candidates.pseudocode: isFirstBarWithLowAboveEma = low[0] > ema(emaLength) && low[1] <= ema(emaLength)[1]; onceTriggered, entryStopLevel = min(entryStopLevel, low[0]) each bar until filled
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop, trailed down one tick below each subsequent bar's low until filled

complexity.reason: a persistent, ratcheting pending-order level carried across bars, not a single-bar stop test

notes: Related to R08-25 (EmaGapBarAsCountertrendStrength), which uses the same EMA-gap-bar concept as a filter rather than an entry trigger.

candidates.name: SecondEmaGapBarRetryEntry
candidates.quote: Sometimes they will get stopped out by the market moving above the signal bar, and if that happens, they will try one more time to reenter their shorts at one tick below the low of the prior bar. Once filled, the signal bar is a second moving average gap bar short signal.
candidates.description: If the R06-09 short is stopped out, re-enter short one tick below the low of the next qualifying bar (a second EMA gap bar).
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop below the second signal bar's low

complexity.reason: needs the prior trade's stopped-out state remembered across bars, plus the EMA

candidates.name: EmaGapReversalFadeInRange
candidates.quote: if it then sells off to below the moving average but is followed by a strong bull reversal bar with a high that is below the moving average, traders will often go long above that bar if there enough room between the high of that bar and the moving average for a long scalp
candidates.description: In a trading-range day, after price dips below the EMA and a strong bull reversal bar closes with its high still below the EMA, buy above that bar for a scalp back to the EMA, provided enough room remains.
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] < ema(emaLength) && bullReversalBar[0] && (ema(emaLength) - high[0]) >= minScalpTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal bar

complexity.reason: EMA plus a single-bar reversal test and a room-to-target check

candidates.name: MovingAverageScalpTarget
candidates.quote: Another common gap is between the high or low of a bar and the moving average. In trends, these can set up good swing trades that test the extreme of the trend, and in trading ranges, they often set up scalps to the moving average.
candidates.description: Exit/take profit on a scalp position when price reaches the EMA.
candidates.book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the moving average

complexity.reason: needs the EMA value each bar

candidates.name: IslandTopReversalEntry
candidates.quote: if there is a bull trend and then there is a gap up that is followed by a gap down on the next bar or even a dozen bars later, the bars between the two gaps are considered to be the island top
candidates.description: After a bull gap up is followed within maxIslandBars bars by a bear gap down whose range does not overlap the first gap (an island top), enter/hold short on a retest of the island's bottom (the bear gap's top).
candidates.pseudocode: gap1 = low[i] > high[i-1]; gap2 = high[j] < low[j-1] (j > i, j - i <= maxIslandBars) && low[j-1] > high[i]; islandBottom = high[j]; high[0] <= islandBottom + toleranceTicks * tickSize (retest, short entry)
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop/limit at the retest of the island bottom

complexity.reason: needs two remembered gap events and a non-overlap test between them, persisting across the island's bar count

notes: Book cross-references Chapter 18, Figure 18.4 for a canonical island-bottom example.

candidates.name: MagnetProximityIncreasesReversalOdds
candidates.quote: The closer the market gets to any magnet, the stronger the magnetic field and the more likely the market will reach the magnet (this is the basis for buy and sell vacuums).
candidates.description: Context filter: weight reversal/target-completion entries more heavily as price gets within nearTicks of a known magnet level (an unfilled gap midpoint, breakout point, or similar remembered level).
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (confidence weighting, not an order by itself)

complexity.reason: 'magnet' and 'vacuum' are qualitative; a design decision is needed on which remembered levels count and how proximity should weight other signals

notes: Chapter 10 (Other Magnets) is the fuller treatment; this chapter's contribution is only the proximity-increases-odds framing.

candidates.name: AggressiveMicroGapLimitEntry
candidates.quote: Once the breakout bar closes, an aggressive trader can place a limit order to buy one tick above the high of the prior bar and risk just three ticks or so.
candidates.description: Immediately after a breakout trend bar closes (per R06-04), place an aggressive limit entry one tick above the high of the bar before the breakout bar, with a tight fixed-tick stop.
candidates.book_order_type: buy limit one tick above the bar-before-the-breakout's high

complexity.reason: builds directly on the already-identified micro-gap bar; only the tight stop distance is new

notes: Book notes the win rate may be as low as ~40% but the reward multiple compensates; that probability is commentary, not an input.

candidates.name: DoNotFadeFreshBreakoutGap
candidates.quote: Breakout gaps often flip the always-in direction and therefore are an important sign of strength... When a trend is just beginning, it is a mistake to take profits too early. Do not use a reasonable candidate for a breakout gap as a measuring gap.
candidates.description: Filter: for withinBars bars after a fresh breakout gap forms, block countertrend (fade) entries and do not treat the gap's projection as a profit-taking target.

complexity.reason: a bars-since-event window on top of the gap primitive

notes: Distinguishing a 'breakaway' gap from a 'measuring' gap is inherently retrospective per the book; withinBars is a proxy for 'too early.'

rejected.quote: Elliott Wave traders see most of these gaps as being formed by a small wave 4 pullback that is staying above the high of wave 1, and expect a wave 5 to follow.
rejected.reason: Elliott Wave labeling is discretionary pattern interpretation with no stated bar-level test

rejected.quote: The FAS on the left traded 16 million shares today, and the RKH on the right traded only 98,000 shares.
rejected.reason: compares two different ticker symbols on the same chart; the engine trades one instrument's own bars

chapter_summary: Extends Chapter 8's measured-move machinery by broadening 'gap' to include ordinary trend bars, open-versus-prior-close gaps, and moving-average gaps, and by classifying gaps as breakaway/measuring/exhaustion only in hindsight. Produces primitives (true gap, open-above-close gap, trend-bar-as-gap) and a general micro-measuring-gap Exit target that generalizes R08's breakout-specific versions; several Entry filters govern when a gap-based target should be trusted (range-so-far vs. ADR, leg-height fraction of ADR, don't-fade-a-fresh-breakout-gap); a family of moving-average-gap-bar Entries (first/second MA gap bar fade, range fade to the MA) introduce trailing/retry pending-order state, graded hard; and an island-reversal Entry and a magnet-proximity context filter round it out. Figures 6.1-6.5 are almost entirely bar-by-bar chart narration restating the same handful of gap/breakout-test/measured-move ideas already captured as candidates; only two passages were pure discretion (Elliott Wave, a cross-symbol volume comparison) and are rejected.
